correctness.rationale: For the quotient by constants, every signal decomposes into adjacent prefix-step differences, so the exact operator seminorm is the maximum variation of expected prefix images. Given a deterministic a-label assignment, the prefix ones occupy at most a contiguous block per packet in label-sorted order, giving ≤2a−1 jumps. Positive packet probabilities let one choose three quarter/half probes in every packet, and Hoeffding bounds force each ideal jump with probability 1−O(a exp(−np_*²/32)), proving matching limit and explicit lower bound. The two-packet prefix image is computed by exact binomial double sum, and independent rational arithmetic verified every 2≤n≤7, including sharp C_7=67/64 and C_6=29/32. Composition of inverse shuffles gives tensor-product packet labels, while the no-collision event for fixed n tends to one, yielding the uniform-rank averaging operator of zero adjacent-output variation. These are all-limit arguments, not finite-enumeration extrapolations.

value.rationale: A stochastic averaging operator can amplify adjacent path variation even though shuffle distributions mix. The exact packet-count dependent sharp gain, universal independence from fixed bias and first seven-card onset describe a well-motivated noncontractivity phenomenon in a familiar probability operator; the threshold is not an arbitrary toy table.

final_claim: For n-site inverse a-packet biased riffle expectation T_{n,p} acting on real signals modulo constants with adjacent-difference variation, the exact norm is bounded by 2a−1 and tends to 2a−1 as n→∞ for each fixed positive packet probability vector. In the unbiased two-packet case the first norm exceeding one occurs sharply at n=7 with C_7=67/64; for r fixed repeated inverse shuffles have limiting gain 2a^r−1, whereas for n fixed gain tends to zero with r.
limitations: Acts on real scalar signals with adjacent path variation, not total variation distance of distributions or physical forward-shuffle ordering.
Asymptotic sharpness requires a fixed packet probability vector with all entries positive; r→∞ is for fixed deck size n.
residual_risks: Related BV transfer-operator research and older biased-shuffle analyses may contain an equivalent operator norm under alternate vocabulary; bibliographic search is not a novelty certificate.
The 2a−1 limit assumes fixed a, all packet probabilities strictly positive and n→∞; cannot interchange with vanishing packet weights or growing a.
